content: Ventral anterior homeobox 1 (VAX1) is a protein encoded by the VAX1 gene in humans. This gene plays a critical role in the development of the forebrain. Its presence has also been identified in other species, such as mice and Xenopus frogs, indicating a conserved evolutionary function. In these organisms, the expression of VAX1 is restricted to the forebrain, as well as the optic and olfactory regions. The VAX1 gene encodes a transcription factor that contains a homeodomain located between amino acid positions 100 and 159. Additionally, it has an alanine-rich region spanning amino acid positions 216 to 253. Studies on mice have demonstrated that VAX1 is expressed in several key areas, including the palate, the coloboma of the visual system, the basal telencephalon, the optic stalk, and the visual eye fields. In these regions, VAX1 expression occurs in conjunction with other important developmental genes, such as Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) and Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (Bmp4). From a clinical perspective, homozygous mutations in the VAX1 gene in mice have been associated with craniofacial abnormalities, including cleft palate. Furthermore, Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) have identified significant correlations between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the VAX1 gene and non-syndromic cleft conditions in humans. These findings have been validated through replication studies conducted across diverse population groups.
